notes: Sink signature: __cdecl violation_report(int type_id, void* enc_ctx_stack_buf). Each of the 14 callers pushes a type_id (1..0x14 in the DBG_* enum ordering as laid out in .rdata @0x10b2a1d0) and a pointer to an XMM-scrambled context blob prepared on the stack (movaps/xorps sequences visible right before the call). Ghidra decompilation failed for the whole 0x100b5650..0x100b8310 cluster (VMProtect-style anti-decompilation padding + heavy control-flow obfuscation); classification below is derived from IAT xrefs, PEB fs:[0x30] reads, and instruction-level primitives (int 0x2d, pushfd/popfd, GetThreadContext, FindWindowW, etc.) rather than decompiled C. The ID<->string mapping was cross-validated against 8 independent anchors (ID=1 PEB read, ID=2 CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, ID=3 IsDebuggerPresent, ID=4 second PEB read, ID=5 dynamic-resolved NtQuery via GetProcAddress, ID=6 FindWindowW x2 callers, ID=0xb GetThreadContext, ID=0x14 int 0x2d) and the string-table order at 0x10b2a1d0. IDs 7,8,9,10,13,14,15 (OUTPUTDEBUGSTRING, NTSETINFORMATIONTHREAD, DEBUGACTIVEPROCESS, PROCESSFILENAME, RDTSC, QUERYPERFORMANCECOUNTER, GETTICKCOUNT) exist as strings in .rdata but have NO caller of FUN_100b5650 in this build.

vectors.primitive_evidence: SEH-only; pushfd @0x100b7fc7 and popfd @0x100b7fea; no imports; ID slot corresponds to PREFIXHOP in .rdata string order
vectors.brief_description: Instruction-prefix single-step trick: sets TF then executes an instruction with a redundant prefix (e.g. F3/F2/64/65). A real debugger single-steps past the prefix and the trailing opcode separately, breaking the expected exception sequence; no debugger => the SEH handler catches one clean STATUS_SINGLE_STEP.

vectors.primitive_evidence: pushfd @0x100b813b + popfd @0x100b8141 (classic EFLAGS.TF toggle); SEH frame present; no imports; ID slot corresponds to SINGLESTEPEXCEPTION in .rdata string order
vectors.brief_description: Sets the trap flag via pushfd/or [esp],0x100/popfd inside SEH: no debugger => STATUS_SINGLE_STEP is caught by the handler; debugger swallows the exception, and the handler never fires.
